source.title: Unveiling Over-Memorization in Finetuning LLMs for Reasoning Tasks
source.authors: Zhiwen Ruan; Yun Chen; Yutao Hou; Peng Li; Yang Liu; Guanhua Chen

page_placements.theme: Gaps, accuracy, likelihood and robustness are distinct outcomes

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures held-out task accuracy and perplexity during LLM fine-tuning, and varies learning rate, training duration, fine-tuning method, model size, and dataset size. It does not test the specific interventions or setups in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The paper tests over-memorization in supervised LLM fine-tuning on reasoning and other tasks. It does not test fitting random labels, and its test-perplexity measure concerns likelihood of a reference reasoning path, not the generalization-gap measures named in V1–V8. Results about OOD performance, prompt perturbation, diversity, calibration, privacy, and proposed mitigation methods are outside those versions; cited prior-work results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study measures reference-output perplexity and task performance during supervised fine-tuning of pretrained LLMs. None of its experiments tests the interventions or comparisons named in V1–V8. In particular, its use of memorization does not establish random-label fitting capacity (V1) or the effect of removing influential training examples (V8).
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the central finding: during LLM fine-tuning, reference-output test perplexity can rise while task accuracy remains high. The authors report that higher learning rates accelerate onset and prolonged training can induce it at smaller learning rates, across tested tasks, models, fine-tuning methods, and dataset sizes. Their broader conclusion also includes worse robustness, OOD performance, calibration, diversity, and privacy protection, and benefits from checkpoint merging and memorization-aware reweighting. Excessive memorization is their interpretation of these dynamics, rather than a measurement of the memorization constructs in V1 or V8.
record.recipe_differences: Supervised fine-tuning of pretrained LLMs on reasoning and other task data; no random-label memorization experiment or image-classification setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate and training duration affect onset; fine-tuning method, model size, and dataset size also change the reported pattern. The text says larger learning rates bring it on earlier and longer training can induce it even at smaller learning rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Reference-output test perplexity rises while task accuracy or win rate remains high or improves during LLM fine-tuning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: During supervised fine-tuning of pretrained LLMs, declining likelihood of held-out reference outputs can coexist with sustained or improving task performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Epoch-3 and epoch-10 checkpoints achieve GSM8K accuracies of 75.6% and 76.4%, while the latter has 4.52 times the test perplexity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Similar in-domain answer accuracy can conceal substantial differences in reference-output perplexity between fine-tuning checkpoints.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report stronger perplexity increases in larger Qwen2.5 models under higher learning rates, and the perplexity–accuracy divergence across 5K, 30K, and 100K training sets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The divergence between reference-output perplexity and task accuracy during LLM fine-tuning occurs across the tested model and dataset sizes.

record.problems: The main trend plots are figures without exact numerical values in the supplied text; several prose conclusions summarize those plots. HumanEval evaluation is small (164 samples), as the paper notes. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the extracted results. Test perplexity measures likelihood of reference reasoning paths, which can differ from answer correctness.
record.rows_left_out: Left out OOD benchmark comparisons, prompt-perturbation robustness, BoN and Pass@N, calibration, privacy attack, diversity metrics, and mitigation-method comparisons because these measure separate outcomes or interventions rather than the listed versions. Also left out the multi-learning-rate curves in Figures 2–4 and appendix figures where the supplied text gives no recoverable numerical values beyond the extracted statements.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting and comparison of natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and training recipe.
Widening networks beyond the width needed for zero training error and measuring subsequent test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning. AdamW is used without an optimizer comparison.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipes that reduce large-batch penalties. Batch size remains 128.
Effects of adding, configuring, or removing dropout. LoRA dropout is configured but not experimentally varied.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, its association with training–test gaps, and comparison with other generalization measures.
Influence-based memorization scores and retraining after removing highly memorized versus randomly selected examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8, not denials of the reported perplexity–performance divergence. The study cites Feldman and Zhang but does not reproduce their removal experiment. No omitted result in the supplied text bears on a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train these models on fixed random labels or compare random-label held-out accuracy with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Does not sweep one-hidden-layer ReLU width through the interpolation threshold on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected image classifiers or isolate local connectivity.
Uses AdamW in its reported fine-tuning setup; it does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD or test optimizer tuning.
Uses batch size 128; it does not vary batch size or test large-batch generalization.
Does not test dropout as a regularizer or compare dropout and weight decay.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with norm- or margin-based generalization measures.
Does not remove memorized training examples or compare retraining with random-example removal.
